diff-checker.name: Diff Checker
diff-checker.tagline: Spot every change between two texts, instantly.
diff-checker.metaTitle: Diff Checker - Compare Two Texts Online Free | JaurTools
diff-checker.metaDescription: Compare two texts line by line and word by word — see exactly what was added, removed or kept. Free, private, runs in your browser.
diff-checker.keywords: text diff, compare text online, diff checker, text comparison tool, find differences in text
diff-checker.quickAnswer: Paste the original text on the left and the new version on the right. The tool aligns them with a longest-common-subsequence algorithm and highlights added lines in green and removed lines in red, with counts of each — perfect for checking edits, translations, or config changes.
keyFacts: A diff finds the longest common subsequence (LCS) of lines shared by both texts, then marks everything else as added or removed.
This tool diffs line by line: rewording inside a line shows the whole line as changed, which is ideal for documents and code.
Side-by-side view keeps both versions aligned so you can read old and new together.
Whitespace matters: a trailing space makes two lines technically different — normalize spacing before comparing if needed.
Large inputs are capped at 500 lines per side to keep the comparison instant in the browser.
The algorithm behind this tool — longest common subsequence — belongs to the same family of ideas as Unix diff and git diff.
howTo: Paste the original text in the left box and the modified text in the right box.
Differences appear instantly — no button needed.
Green rows are lines added in the new version; red rows are lines removed from the old one.
Use Swap to flip the two sides, Sample to see a demo, or Clear to start over.
Read the counts above the table for a quick summary of how much changed.
For long documents, compare one section at a time to keep the table easy to read.
diff-checker.formula:
LCS(i,j) = LCS(i+1,j+1) + 1        if line i == line j
LCS(i,j) = max(LCS(i+1,j), LCS(i,j+1))  otherwise
Backtrack from (0,0): follow matches, emit deletions/additions on the way.
diff-checker.workedExample:
Left (4 lines):
The quick brown fox / jumps over / the lazy dog / and runs away
Right (5 lines):
The quick brown fox / leaps over / the lazy dog / and walks away / The end
Common subsequence: line 1 and line 3.
Result: 2 unchanged, 2 removed (jumps over, and runs away), 3 added (leaps over, and walks away, The end).
benefits: Instant visual proof of what changed between two drafts.
No uploads: contracts, code, and private documents stay on your device.
Swap and sample buttons make experimenting frictionless.
Clean side-by-side table that works on mobile too.
limitations: Line-based: a single changed word flags the whole line — it does not highlight word-level changes within a line.
Capped at 500 lines per side for browser performance; split bigger files first.
Treats lines as plain text: rich formatting differences are not compared.
A comparison aid, not a merge tool — it cannot combine the two versions for you.
diff-checker.privacyNote: This tool runs 100% in your browser. Your data never leaves your device.

faqs.q: How does the diff algorithm work?
faqs.a: It computes the longest common subsequence (LCS) of the two line sequences with dynamic programming, then walks back through the table emitting unchanged, deleted, and added lines in order.

faqs.q: Why does a tiny edit mark the whole line as changed?
faqs.a: This is a line-based diff, like classic Unix diff. It compares whole lines, so any character change flags the line. Word-level highlighting is a different feature this tool does not include.
Yes — lines must match exactly, including spaces and tabs. If spacing noise pollutes your diff, normalize both texts (e.g. trim trailing spaces) before comparing.
Yes, 500 lines per side. Beyond that the comparison table would slow down the browser, so the tool asks you to split larger files.
